content.value_statement: Invalid data often bypasses a single validation point and fails later in execution. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to add layered checks that make recurring bugs harder to reintroduce.
actual_capabilities: Explains where to place entry-point validation for invalid inputs.
Guides business-logic validation for operation-specific constraints.
Shows how environment guards can prevent dangerous test behavior.
Recommends debug logging to trace validation failures.
Provides a repeatable workflow for tracing data flow and checkpoints.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not an automated static analyzer.
Examples are TypeScript-focused and may need adaptation for other languages.
It does not prove that every code path is covered.
It depends on the user or agent to apply the validation pattern correctly.

use_cases.title: Fix recurring invalid input bugs
use_cases.description: Use the skill to trace where invalid data enters, moves, and causes failures, then add checks at each layer.

use_cases.title: Harden test-only filesystem operations
use_cases.description: Apply environment guards so test helpers cannot accidentally modify source directories or unsafe paths.

use_cases.title: Review validation coverage before release
use_cases.description: Map entry, business, environment, and debug layers to find missing protections before shipping.

prompt_templates.title: Find validation layers for a bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a known invalid input bug.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the defense-in-depth validation pattern on this bug. Trace the bad value, list each layer it crosses, and suggest one validation check per layer.

prompt_templates.title: Add layered validation to a function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this function for invalid input paths. Add entry validation, business logic validation, environment guards, and useful debug logging where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Test bypasses across validation layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tests that try to bypass each validation layer. Show which layer should catch each invalid input and what failure message should appear.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a workflow for structural safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this workflow for defense-in-depth validation. Map every data checkpoint, identify missing guards, and propose minimal changes that make the bug structurally impossible.

output_examples.input: A project setup flow allows an empty directory path and later runs a workspace operation in the wrong location.
output: Entry layer: reject empty or whitespace-only directory values.
Business layer: require a valid project directory before workspace creation.
Environment layer: block unsafe filesystem operations during tests.
Debug layer: log directory, current working directory, and call stack before the operation.

output_examples.input: A test helper can initialize a repository outside the temporary directory.
output_examples.output: The recommended output is a layered fix plan: validate the requested directory, resolve and normalize the path, compare it with the temporary directory in tests, and add targeted regression tests.

output_examples.input: A reviewer wants to know whether one validation check is enough.
output_examples.output: The skill should explain why one check can be bypassed and list additional checkpoints where the same invalid value should be rejected.

best_practices: Trace the invalid value from origin to final use before editing code.
Add the smallest useful validation at each layer instead of one broad check.
Write tests that prove later layers still catch invalid data if earlier layers are bypassed.
anti_patterns: Adding only one validation check and assuming every caller uses it.
Logging sensitive values while adding debug instrumentation.
Using environment guards as a substitute for normal input validation.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is an instructional skill that describes validation patterns and example code.

faq.question: Which languages does it support?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript, but the layered validation approach applies to most programming languages.

faq.question: Is this only for security bugs?
faq.answer: No. It also helps with reliability bugs caused by invalid data, bad paths, or unsafe test setup.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide Claude Code while reviewing a bug, adding validation, or planning regression tests.

faq.question: What are the four layers?
faq.answer: The skill recommends entry validation, business logic validation, environment guards, and debug instrumentation.

faq.question: Does it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It gives a structured review pattern, but a human or agent should still inspect the final code and tests.
